title: Density-aware token and compact-component reference for docs site
creator: Ava Rodriguez
description: Consolidate guidance and example patterns for density-aware design across tokens, buttons, tables, and charts and publish a compact-component reference on the docs site. The goal is to provide engineers and product designers with a single page per component family that explains density profiles (compact / default / spacious), token mappings, accessibility constraints, code snippets for React + CSS variables, migration hints for legacy token names, and a minimal codemod recipe. This ticket focuses on authoring content, example assets, and acceptance criteria; engineering will deliver the codemod and docs rendering changes in ENG-5812 and ENG-6140.
acceptance_criteria: A single docs page for each: tokens (density section), buttons, tables, charts with explicit compact/default/spacious examples
Each component page includes: do/don't micro-gallery (3 examples each), API prop table, token-to-css-variable mapping, and a small 'performance/render-cost' note
Migration notes cover 90% of common legacy token names and include a codemod snippet and example PR link
All code examples compile in the docs playground (React snippets tested) and are linked to the related GitHub PR
Design review sign-off and accessibility check completed (contrast, touch target sizes)
updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting — agreed scope: density profiles + migration notes + compact examples. Design will author all imagery and micro-animations. Engineering to enable component gallery variants (ENG-5812).

2025-02-18: Draft tokens density section completed. Added token mapping table and notes on semantic tokens vs. platform tokens. Shared Figma frames: figma.com/file/RedwoodDensity/compact-profiles (internal).
2025-02-21: Design review — PM asked to add explicit 'when not to use compact' guidance for tables and charts. Added new do/don't examples for data-dense and touch-first contexts.

2025-02-26: PR placeholder opened: github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1425 with initial markdown structure and code snippets. Engineering requested simpler CSS-variable examples for teams using plain CSS without React.
2025-03-01: Accessibility pass started; discovered compact-table row height falls below 44px on mobile — added note to avoid below 44px and added alternate responsive pattern.
2025-03-04: Submitted updated draft to docs review board. Waiting for review from content and eng reviewers. Linked ENG tickets for codemod and rendering.
reviewer_notes: PM (Hannah Cho): Emphasize migration impact to Dedicated customers. Add example of client-side override patterns.
Engineering (Diego Nguyen): Provide both CSS variable and inline-style JS examples; include small note about runtime token substitution in Private deployments.
Accessibility (Maya Singh): Confirm contrast for compact labels and ensure 44px touch target minimum is documented for mobile breakpoints.
migration_plan: Step 1: Publish docs with a clear token mapping table and 'rename affordances' section
Step 2: Merge codemod (ENG-6140) with a dry-run mode and link to the PR from the docs page
Step 3: Run a small internal campaign to notify integrators and include a changelog entry in release notes
Step 4: Add a quick 'revert-to-legacy' snippet for customers that need gradual rollout
dev_notes: Provide 3 variants per component in the docs code sandbox: compact, default, spacious
Include a CSS snippet mapping semantic tokens to --rw- variables (example included in markdown)
Keep the React examples free of platform-specific wrappers so partner teams can copy-paste quickly
